what_it_measured.text: The Synthetic Melanocortin Agonist NDP-MSH Ameliorates THSD7A-Associated Membranous Nephropathy in an Active Immunization Mouse Model

dose.text: To test the efficacy of the nonsteroidogenic pan-MCR agonist NDP-MSH [22], immunized mice were randomly assigned to receive daily subcutaneous injections of NDP-MSH (customsynthesized peptide from GL Biochem Ltd., Boston, MA, USA) at an equal dose (0.7 μmol/kg body weight per day) or an equal volume of vehicle (PBS) from weeks 7 to 9.

route.text: To assess the effects of the NDP-MSH on T cells, mice were randomly assigned to receive daily subcutaneous injections of NDP- MSH at an equal dose (0.7 μmol/kg body weight per day) or an equal volume of PBS vehicle for 3 weeks.

To test the efficacy of the nonsteroidogenic pan-MCR agonist NDP-MSH [22], immunized mice were randomly assigned to receive daily subcutaneous injections of NDP-MSH (customsynthesized peptide from GL Biochem Ltd., Boston, MA, USA) at an equal dose (0.7 μmol/kg body weight per day) or an equal volume of vehicle (PBS) from weeks 7 to 9.

endpoint.text: Notably, this partial remission of proteinuria was accompanied by a marked improvement in glomerular histopathology, as assessed by electron microscopy, including pronounced attenuation of GBM thickening, substantial resolution of podocyte foot process effacement, and a significant reduction in subepithelial electron-dense immune deposits in NDP-MSH– treated mice (Figure 2D).

After 2 weeks of treatment, NDP-MSH–treated mice exhibited a statistically significant reduction in albuminuria compared with PBS-treated controls, with an approximately 42.3% decrease, as demonstrated by urine protein electrophoresis (Figure 2B) and quantified by the urinary albumintocreatinine ratio (Figure 2C).

3.2 | Delayed NDP-MSH Treatment Attenuates Albuminuria and Glomerular Injury in THSD7A-Associated MN Having established a clinically relevant model, we next evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of melanocortin therapy using the synthetic melanocortin receptor agonist NDP-MSH (Figure 2A).
